origin.description: Uses direct plug-in methodology to select the bin width of a histogram.
origin.usage:
dpih(x, scalest = "minim", level = 2L, gridsize = 401L,
     range.x = range(x), truncate = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector containing the sample on which the histogram is to be constructed.

arguments.name: scalest
arguments.text: Estimate of scale: "stdev", "iqr" (interquartile range divided by 1.349), or "minim" (the smaller of those two).

arguments.name: level
arguments.text: Number of levels of functional estimation used in the plug-in rule.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of grid points used in the binned approximations to functional estimates.

arguments.name: range.x
arguments.text: Range over which functional estimates are obtained. The default is the minimum and maximum data values.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If TRUE, observations outside range.x are omitted. Otherwise they weight the extreme grid points.

origin.details: Unknown functionals in the expression for the asymptotically optimal bin width are replaced by kernel estimates. The normal distribution provides the initial estimate.

translation.description: Uses direct plug-in methodology to select the bin width of a histogram.
translation.usage:
dpih(x, scalest="minim", level=2, gridsize=401,
     range_x=None, truncate=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric sample on which the histogram is to be constructed.

arguments.name: scalest
arguments.text: Estimate of scale: "stdev", "iqr" (interquartile range divided by 1.349), or "minim" (the smaller of those two).

arguments.name: level
arguments.text: Number of levels of functional estimation used in the plug-in rule. An integer from 0 to 5. The default is 2.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of grid points used in the binned approximations to functional estimates.

arguments.name: range_x
arguments.text: The two endpoints over which functional estimates are obtained. This is range.x in R. None uses the minimum and maximum data values.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If true, observations outside range_x are omitted. Otherwise they weight the extreme grid points.

translation.details: Unknown functionals in the expression for the asymptotically optimal bin width are replaced by kernel estimates from bkfe. Bin counts come from the Rust crate linbin. The normal distribution provides the initial estimate.
translation.example:
from mass import geyser
from kernsmooth import dpih
from kernsmooth.dpih import histogram_breaks
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = geyser["duration"]
h = dpih(x)
plt.hist(x, bins=histogram_breaks(x, h))
